newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, bellies end sharply higher, cash lifts.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, bellies end sharply higher, cash lifts.

text.p: CME nearby hog futures soared to limit gains and a 2-1/2 week high in response to higher-than-expected cash hog prices, floor traders said.
Pork bellies also settled sharply higher on cash-connected buying, traders said.

Tight supplies of market-ready hogs pushed cash prices beyond initial projections early, and hogs sold in some areas as much as $1.50 per cwt higher after traders had been looking for steady prices, cash-connected sources said.
Packers were said to be cutting back on their Saturday operations, but some saw it as a supply, rather than a demand factor.
"A small kill on Saturday says to me that there aren't enough hogs to kill," the trader said.
The pool of buy-orders in the December contract was estimated at 200 contracts, pit traders said.

Heavy commodity fund short-covering was a big feature in hog futures, traders said. The market penetrated several key levels of resistance that spurred funds and technical traders to get out of short positions, they said.
Packers Trading was an early buyer and FIMAT Futures Inc, a late buyer, sources said. Rand Financial was a late seller.

Cash-connected buying in the pork belly pit pushed that market sharply higher, traders said. Other bullish factors included expectations for a lower-than-year ago slaughter, traders and analysts said.

USDA estimated Friday's slaughter at 358,000 head. That figure fell below analysts' earlier expectations, which ranged from 361,000 to 366,000 head. USDA tabbed this week's overall hog slaughter at 1,851,000 head, slightly up from 1,835,000 a week ago but down from 2,002,000 a year ago.

December live hogs settled up 1.50 at 55.90 cents a lb and February was up 1.825 at 75.975 cent cents. Other months were settled up 0.400 to up 1.275 cent. February pork bellies closed up 2.300 cent at 70.600 cents a lb, with other months up 0.500 to up 2.300 cent.
